construct: AVPR2 encodes the basolateral vasopressin V2 receptor in collecting-duct principal cells. Normal V2-receptor activation stimulates Gs, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and PKA, leading to apical insertion of AQP2 water channels; AVPR2 loss of function disrupts this pathway and prevents urinary concentration.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Lifelong polyuria/hypernatremia, persistently dilute urine without desmopressin response, and AVPR2 loss identify X-linked nephrogenic DI from failed V2-receptor Gs-cAMP-PKA signaling and apical AQP2 insertion.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: NKCC2 and urea recycling contribute to urine concentration, but they do not explain the receptor-specific failure to respond to desmopressin. Aldosterone/ENaC and angiotensin-II hemodynamics are different renal pathways.
